translation: Zhongjing's Shanghan Lun states: "In wind stroke, [the patient] can eat; in cold damage, [the patient] cannot eat. In both, the mouth is harmonious within and [the patient] does not hate food." If there is injury from toil, and loss of regulation in food and drink, and discomfort in cold and warmth, in all three [the patient] hates food, the mouth does not know the five flavors, nor does it know the flavor of the five grains. This single differentiation suffices to divide the two patterns of internal[injury] excess-insufficiency and external[injury] excess-insufficiency. Although in the cold-damage pattern [the patient] cannot eat, he does not hate food; the mouth is harmonious [within], and he knows the five flavors and also knows the flavor of grain. Because without the internal pattern, the heart qi is harmonious and the spleen qi communicates, and [the patient] knows the flavors of the five grains.
